heading: INTEGRATED SERVICES FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN EMPOWERMENT
translated_text:
INTEGRATED SERVICES FOR WOMEN AND CHILDREN EMPOWERMENT

REGENT OF LAMANDAU

PROVINCE OF CENTRAL KALIMANTAN

heading: REGIONAL REGULATION OF LAMANDAU REGENCY
CHAPTER I
translated_text:
CHAPTER I

GENERAL PROVISIONS

Article 1

In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by:
1. Region is Lamandau Regency.
2. Regional Government is the administration of Government affairs by the Regional Government and the Regional House of Representatives according to the principles of Autonomy and Co-Administration with the principle of the widest possible autonomy within the system and principles of the Unitary State of the Republic of Indonesia as referred to in the 1945 Constitution.
3. Regional Government is the Regent together with Regional Apparatus as Elements of Regional Government Administration.
4. Regent is the Regent of Lamandau.
5. Regional House of Representatives is the Regional House of Representatives of Lamandau Regency.
6. Regional Secretary is the Regional Secretary of Lamandau Regency.
7. Child is a person who has not reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, and is not yet married, including a child who is still in the womb.
8. Woman is every person who is physically born as a woman.
9. Victim is a woman and or child who experiences misery and or suffering either directly or indirectly as a result of an act of violence.
10. Prevention is all efforts carried out by government or non-government institutions aimed at providing a sense of security to women and children.
11. Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security to victims carried out by the government, family, advocates, social institutions or other community institutions, police, prosecutors, courts or other parties either temporarily or based on court decisions or determinations, in connection with acts of violence against children and women.
12. Child Protection is all activities carried out to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human rights and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
13. Women's Protection is all activities carried out to guarantee and protect women and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human rights and dignity, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
14. Misery is any act that results in or may result in suffering whether psychological, physical, sexual, economic, social to the victim.
15. Physical violence is any act that causes pain, injury, wounds or disability to a person's body, miscarriage, fainting and or causes death.
16. Psychological violence is an act that causes fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness and or severe psychological suffering to women and or children.
17. Sexual violence is any act in the form of sexual harassment, forced sexual intercourse with another person for commercial purposes and or certain purposes.
18. Service is an action taken as soon as possible to the victim, when seeing, hearing and knowing of the impending, ongoing or after occurrence of violence against the victim.
19. Companion is a person or institution that has the ability to provide assistance to victims to conduct counseling, therapy, legal services and advocacy, for strengthening victim recovery.
20. Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection to women and children victims in accordance with the standard operating procedures or abbreviated as SOP that are determined.
21. Community is individuals, families, groups, social organizations and or other community organizations.
22. Integrated Service Center for Women and Children Empowerment hereinafter abbreviated as P2TP2A is one form of service facility for women and children in an effort to fulfill information and needs in the fields of education, health, economy, politics, law, protection and prevention of acts of violence and trafficking against women and children.

heading: CHAPTER II
Article 3
translated_text:
Article 3

The objectives of implementing integrated services for women and children empowerment are:
a. To guarantee the fulfillment of the rights of women and children in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
b. To prevent and protect women and children against violence.
c. To encourage the community to carry out their obligations in the prevention and protection of women and children in accordance with applicable laws and regulations.
d. To restore victims as a result of acts of violence experienced.
e. To take action against perpetrators of domestic violence.
f. To provide disaggregated data by sex and information on issues of empowerment and protection of women and children for the community who need it.
g. To encourage the provision of facilities, infrastructure and various types of services in various areas of life for women and children such as data and information centers, counseling, psychological and medical therapy, assistance, education and training, referral centers, skills training and so on as an effort to improve the quality of life of women, welfare and protection of children managed by the community independently.

heading: CHAPTER III
Article 5
Article 6
Article 7
Article 8
translated_text:
Article 8

1. Physical violence is an act that results in pain, illness, or serious injury.
2. Psychological violence is an act that results in fear, loss of self-confidence, loss of ability to act, feelings of helplessness, and/or severe psychological suffering in a person. (3) Sexual violence includes:
a. Forced sexual relations committed against a person residing within the household scope.
b. Forced sexual relations against one person within the household scope with another person for commercial purposes and/or certain purposes.
3. Household neglect is an act of not providing livelihood, not providing care, or not providing maintenance to persons within the household scope.
4. Neglect also applies to any person who causes economic dependence by restricting and/or prohibiting decent work inside or outside the home so that the victim is under the control of that person.

heading: Article 9
translated_text:
Article 9

1. The state, government, community, family, and parents have the obligation and responsibility for the implementation of child protection.
2. The government is responsible for efforts to prevent domestic violence.

heading: Article 10
translated_text:
Article 10

1. The state, government, community, family, and parents have the obligation and responsibility for the implementation of child protection.
2. The government is responsible for efforts to prevent domestic violence.
3. Every person who hears, sees or knows of the occurrence of domestic violence is obliged to make efforts in accordance with their capacity to:
a. Prevent the continuation of criminal acts;
b. Provide protection to victims;
c. Provide emergency assistance; and
d. Assist in the process of submitting an application for protection order.

heading: CHAPTER IV
translated_text:
CHAPTER IV

IMPLEMENTATION OF CHILD PROTECTION AND VICTIMS OF DOMESTIC VIOLENCE

heading: Article 11
translated_text:
Article 11

1. Every child receives protection to worship according to their religion.
2. Before the child can determine their choice, the religion embraced by the child follows the religion of their parents.
3. The state, government, community, family, parents, guardians, and social institutions guarantee the protection of children in embracing their religion.
4. Protection of children in embracing their religion includes fostering, guiding, and practicing religious teachings for children.

heading: Article 12
translated_text:
Article 12

1. The Government is obliged to provide facilities and organize comprehensive health efforts for children, so that every child obtains an optimal degree of health from the womb.
2. Comprehensive health efforts include promotive, preventive, curative and rehabilitative services for both basic health services and referrals.
3. Parents and families are responsible for maintaining the health of children and caring for children from the womb.
4. The State, government, families and parents are obliged to protect children from acts of:
a. Removal of children's organs and/or children's body tissues without regard to the health of the child;
b. Sale and purchase of organs and/or children's body tissues; and
c. Health research that uses children as research subjects without parental consent and does not prioritize the best interests of the child.

heading: Article 13
Article 14
Article 15
translated_text:
Article 15

The Government and other state institutions are obliged and responsible to provide special protection to children in emergency situations, children in conflict with the law, children from minority and isolated groups, children exploited economically and/or sexually, children who are trafficked, children who are victims of narcotics, alcohol, psychotropic and other addictive substances (napza) abuse, children who are victims of kidnapping, sale and trafficking, children who are victims of violence both physical and/or mental, children with disabilities, and children who are victims of maltreatment and neglect.

heading: Article 16
translated_text:
Article 16

1. Within 1x24 (one times twenty-four) hours from knowing or receiving a report of domestic violence, the police must immediately provide temporary protection to the victim.
2. Temporary protection is provided for a maximum of 7 (seven) days from the time the victim is received or handled.
3. Within 1x24 (one times twenty-four) hours from the provision of protection, the police must request a protection order decree from the court.

heading: Article 17
translated_text:
Article 17

In providing temporary protection, the police may cooperate with health workers, social workers, volunteer companions, and/or spiritual counselors to accompany the victim.

heading: Article 18
translated_text:
Article 18

The police must provide information to the victim about the victim's right to receive services and assistance.

heading: Article 19
translated_text:
Article 19

The police must immediately conduct an investigation after knowing or receiving a report about the occurrence of domestic violence.

heading: Article 20
translated_text:
Article 20

The police immediately convey to the victim about:
a. The identity of the officer for introduction to the victim;
b. Domestic violence is a crime against human dignity; and
c. The obligation of the police to protect the victim.

heading: Article 21
translated_text:
Article 21

In providing health services to victims, health workers must:
a. Examine the health of the victim in accordance with their professional standards;
b. Make a written report of the examination results of the victim and visum et repertum at the request of the police investigator or a medical certificate that has the same legal force as evidence.

heading: Article 22
Article 23
Article 24
translated_text:
Article 24

In providing services, spiritual counselors must provide explanations regarding rights, obligations and provide strengthening of faith and piety to the victim.

heading: Article 25
translated_text:
Article 25

In providing protection and services, advocates are obliged to:
a. Provide legal consultation that includes information regarding the victim's rights and the judicial process;
b. Accompany the victim at the investigation, prosecution, and examination levels in court hearings and assist the victim to completely describe the domestic violence they experienced; and
c. Coordinate with fellow law enforcers, volunteer companions, and social workers so that the judicial process proceeds as it should.

heading: Article 26
translated_text:
Article 26

1. Victims have the right to report domestic violence directly to the police either at the place where the victim is located or at the scene of the case.
2. Victims may authorize family members or other persons to report domestic violence to the police either at the place where the victim is located or at the scene of the case.
3. In the event the victim is a child, the report may be made by the parent, guardian, caregiver, or the child concerned which is carried out in accordance with the provisions of applicable laws and regulations.

heading: Article 27
translated_text:
Article 27

The Chief Judge within a period of 7 (seven) days from receipt of the application must issue a decree containing a protection order for the victim and other family members, unless there are valid reasons.

heading: Article 28
Article 30
translated_text:
Article 30

Upon the application of the victim or their representative, the court may consider:
a. Establishing a special condition;
b. Amending or canceling a special condition of the protection order.

heading: Article 31
translated_text:
Article 31

1. A protection order may be granted for a period of no more than 1 (one) year.
2. A protection order may be extended by court order.
3. An application for extension of a protection order shall be submitted 7 (seven) days before the expiration of its validity period.

heading: Article 32
translated_text:
Article 32

1. The court may declare one or more additional protection orders.
2. In granting additional protection orders, the court shall consider statements from the victim, health workers, social workers, support volunteers, and/or spiritual counselors.

heading: Article 33
translated_text:
Article 33

1. Based on consideration of potential danger, the court may declare one or more additional conditions in the protection order.
2. In granting additional conditions in the protection order, the court shall consider statements from the victim, health workers, social workers, support volunteers, and/or spiritual counselors.

heading: Article 34
translated_text:
Article 34

1. The Police may arrest and subsequently detain without a warrant a perpetrator believed to have violated a protection order, even if the violation did not occur at the place where the police officer is stationed.
2. The arrest and detention as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be accompanied by a warrant of arrest and detention after 1x24 (one times twenty-four) hours.
3. Suspension of detention shall not apply to detention as referred to in paragraphs (1) and (2).

heading: Article 35
translated_text:
Article 35

1. To provide protection to the victim, the Police may arrest the perpetrator with sufficient preliminary evidence for having violated a protection order.
2. The arrest as referred to in paragraph (1) may be followed by detention accompanied by a detention order within 1x24 (one times twenty-four) hours.

heading: Article 36
translated_text:
Article 36

1. The victim, the Police or support volunteers may submit a written report regarding an alleged violation of a protection order.
2. In the event the court receives a written report as referred to in paragraph (1), the perpetrator shall be ordered to appear within 3x24 (three times twenty-four) hours for examination.
3. The examination as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be conducted by the court at the place where the perpetrator previously lived with the victim at the time the violation is alleged to have occurred.

heading: Article 37
translated_text:
Article 37

1. If the court finds that the perpetrator has violated a protection order and is suspected of committing further violations, the court may require the perpetrator to make a written statement containing a commitment to comply with the protection order.
2. If the perpetrator continues to disregard the written statement as referred to in paragraph (1), the court may detain the perpetrator for a maximum of 30 days.
3. The detention as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be accompanied by a detention order.

heading: CHAPTER V
translated_text:
CHAPTER V

VICTIM RECOVERY

Article 38

For the purpose of recovery, victims may obtain services from:
a. Health workers;
b. Social workers;
c. Support volunteers; and
d. Spiritual counselors.

heading: Article 39
translated_text:
Article 39

1. Health workers shall examine victims in accordance with their professional standards.
2. In the event the victim requires treatment, health workers shall restore and rehabilitate the victim's health.

heading: Article 40
translated_text:
Article 40

Social workers, support volunteers, and/or spiritual counselors shall provide services to victims in the form of counseling to strengthen and/or provide a sense of security for the victim.

heading: CHAPTER VI
translated_text:
CHAPTER VI

INSTITUTIONAL ARRANGEMENTS

Article 41

1. In the context of providing protection services to women and children who are victims of violence, the Regional Government shall establish P2TP2A.
2. The membership of P2TP2A as referred to in (1) shall consist of:
a. regional government elements;
b. community elements; and
c. academic elements.
3. The membership of P2TP2A as referred to in paragraph (2) shall be established by Regent's Decree.

heading: Article 42
translated_text:
Article 42

1. The Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) shall facilitate the provision of various services for the community, both physical and non-physical, including information, referrals, consultation/counseling, skills training and other activities.
2. The Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) may also serve as a venue for conducting training for cadres who have a strong commitment and concern for women's and children's issues in all fields (health, education, economy, politics, law and protection of women and children from violence and human trafficking) so that they can work together and participate in providing services to the community within a framework of improving the quality of life and protection for women and children.

heading: Article 43
translated_text:
Article 43

Programs that may be carried out by the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) include:
a. Women's empowerment.
b. Protection of women and children from violence and human trafficking.
c. Communication, information and education.
d. Increasing community member participation.
e. Capacity building for managers.

heading: Article 44
translated_text:
Article 44

The success indicators of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) are as follows:
a. The establishment and functioning of the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) that provides women's empowerment services, protection of women and children in the fields of law, politics, education, health, economy, violence and human trafficking.
b. An increase in the number of women and children utilizing the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A).
c. An increase in the number of women and children receiving training.
d. The functioning of dialogue and communication mechanisms among government, community and the business sector.
e. Cooperation between the Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) with government and the business sector.

heading: CHAPTER VII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VII

REPORTING

Article 45

1. The Integrated Service Center for the Empowerment of Women and Children (P2TP2A) shall report the implementation of activities to the Regent.
2. The submission of a written report as referred to in paragraph (1) shall be carried out at least once every 3 (three) months.

heading: CHAPTER VIII
translated_text:
CHAPTER VIII

FINANCING

Article 46

Financing for the implementation of the Integrated Service for the Empowerment of Women and Children shall be sourced from:
a. The regional revenue and expenditure budget of Lamandau Regency.
b. Other legitimate and non-binding sources.

heading: CHAPTER IX
translated_text:
CHAPTER IX

CLOSING PROVISIONS

Article 47

This Regional Regulation shall come into force on the date of promulgation.

In order that everyone may know of it, the promulgation of this Regional Regulation is ordered by its placement in the Regional Gazette of Lamandau Regency.

on 6 July 2015

heading: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF LAMANDAU REGENCY
translated_text:
ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF LAMANDAU REGENCY

NUMBER 16 OF 2015 CONCERNING INTEGRATED SERVICES FOR THE EMPOWERMENT OF WOMEN AND CHILDREN

heading: I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION
heading_path: ELUCIDATION OF REGIONAL REGULATION OF LAMANDAU REGENCY
translated_text:
I. GENERAL ELUCIDATION

All forms of violence in general and acts of violence against women and or children are a form of violation of human rights and constitute a form of crime against human dignity as well as discriminatory treatment, therefore it is the obligation of the Government and Regional Government to realize the guarantee of security/protection of honor, dignity, property, freedom from torture, or treatment that degrades human dignity and discriminatory treatment.

Current developments show that there are still frequent acts of violence against women and or children within the family environment and within society which clearly result in misery and suffering of women and or children physically, psychologically, or sexually including threats of certain actions, coercion, or deprivation of rights..

Services and handling, guidance and empowerment of women and or children have not been optimal so far. Various causes mentioned above are that most women and or children victims of violence choose to remain silent and their problems end with women and children falling into powerlessness.

This regional regulation is intended as an effort by the Government of Lamandau Regency to meet the demands of society by providing services for the rights of women and children victims of violence in a comprehensive, clear and firm manner to protect or side with victims.
